title: Slim's guitar clamp, the Apollo-style show finale and his dress
summary: Slim could not play without his clamp so the trumpet player modulated to D-flat; Schiffman insisted on suits and Slim idolised Gatemouth.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: But Slim with his guitar, he had a clamp. He didn't know how to play without the clamp, the choke on it. He couldn't play without it, right? And T-Bone Walker tried to get him to change his style, you know, but he didn't take the time to do it. But with his amplifier on, trying to find the key. So the trumpet player, he made a modulation for everybody to go to D-flat. That's the only thing that saved us on the stage at times. So Schiffman said, no, we can't use this for finality. That's the end of the show. Charlie Bonnet, you know, they were in the background. The screen was behind them. And when they modulated to D-flat, then the curtain was opened up and the big band would come on up. And everybody would be for the finale, you see. But Slim couldn't, by him not knowing how to get to D-flat, where D-flat was, he had to hear it. He'd find out where it was.
You mentioned there was a screen. What was it? The screen?

No, a curtain. The curtain was up. The curtain was up like that, you know. While we were playing the curtain was up. So you couldn't see the big band in the back, just who was featured on the front, us. And then when the guy made the modulation, then the curtain was up, and then the big band would come up for the finale.
Was Mr. Schiffman very particular about the bands and how they were formed? Your parents. Your parents had to be?

Because Slim, if you didn't have any uniform, he'd send you downtown. The man, the tailor shop, he'd send you down there and you'd go get the uniform. You'd even have to get rent them or whatever. Because Slim wanted to do a, I forget the name, Morning, some kind of song that he sang. And he wanted to come out there with his coveralls on. He did it one time, but Schiffman didn't want to let him do it no more. He said, no, you come here, you dress up. You put on some kind of suit. And he wore some fabulous things. Because his idol was, what's that man, Gate Mouth. Oh, Gate, sure. Gate Mouth was his idol, see. So anything Gate did, he tried to emulate. But he couldn't do it, you see. Because he didn't have the finesse that Gate had, see, because Gate walked that board. And he made a song about Gate walked the board. He couldn't do it. He just didn't know how to do that. And we were in Texas, that's what I wanted to say. The first time I think they started packaging groups, when they had Guitar Slim, T-Bone Walker, and Joe Turner. We went through Texas, and we tore it up with those people. Because people want to see. Because once upon a time, it was one artist. Yeah. One artist could go to town and draw people like flies. But then, I don't know what happened. People decided, hey, we better package up something. I think we were the first ones to start the packaging thing.
